Extended remediation notes

  1. URGENT: Observed installed or operator-reported PHP version below the upstream fixes. Patch all relevant running web SAPIs, not only the CLI binary. Confirm vendor backports where applicable.
  2. Review Dockerfiles, CI and deployment manifests naming versions below the fixes. Verify actual deployed image digest/runtime before assigning vulnerability status.
  3. Immediately prioritize internet-reachable mod_php and other web-facing PHP (FPM, CGI, FrankenPHP, LiteSpeed). Determine network reachability separately; this is NOT an external exposure scan.
  4. Apply upstream PHP 8.5.12 / 8.4.27 / 8.3.36 / 8.2.35 or your vendor's verified equivalent patches. Restart/recycle all PHP workers, pools and services; re-scan and verify the active web-serving SAPI and container images.
  5. If patching must be delayed: consider administratively enforced memory_limit=-1, conservative post_max_size and edge request bounds for CVE-2026-109618; these are incomplete risk reductions and have availability tradeoffs.
  6. For CVE-2026-109619, administratively disable session.upload_progress.enabled and restart all workers; on PHP 8.5, consider fatal_error_backtraces=0 until patched. Neither measure covers every attack path.
  7. Confirm WAF/origin access cannot be bypassed and document time-bounded restrictions if a patch cannot be deployed immediately.
  8. Preserve and review access/error logs and EDR telemetry from before patching; patched servers may already have been compromised. A clean IOC result does not rule out compromise.
  9. See official advisories: https://www.php.net/ and https://github.com/php/php-src/security/advisories/GHSA-w8hw-w9fx-j79w and https://github.com/php/php-src/security/advisories/GHSA-6wmf-4rv5-p3rp
Compromise investigation (attempts, coverage, signed IOCs)

Exploitation attempts: NOT_ASSESSED  ·  Possible compromise: NOT_ASSESSED  ·  Investigation coverage: NOT_REQUESTED

Statuses are independent. This tool never claims a host is clean or confirmed compromised. Long request-target length, large HTTP bodies, unusual form-field names, and multipart nesting are distinct signals; ordinary access logs typically provide only the first (URI length heuristic). Blocked WAF actions are not successful exploitation. WAF leads do not alone set possible-compromise. Do not claim two requests shared a PHP worker without worker identity evidence.

Configured SAPI hints: Observed configured/inventory hints: PHP-FPM (binary/package/process or FastCGI proxy hints). These artifacts do NOT prove which SAPI currently serves HTTP. Research note: mod_php may continue into request shutdown / worker reuse after some startup fatals; PHP-FPM typically terminates the worker on request-startup failure but can still be exploited after successful startup (application-dependent decode and upload-progress paths). Do not infer that PHP-FPM cannot be exploited. Patch and verify the active serving runtime separately.
HTTP body / form metadata: Not available from ordinary access logs. Prefer offline WAF exports with documented fields. Content-Length and multipart nesting are not inferred from URI lines.
Observed PHP configuration: Whitelisted php.ini settings are static text only (OBSERVED≠EFFECTIVE). Temporary mitigations such as session.upload_progress.enabled or memory_limit changes are unverified and do not replace patching.
